chapter: Washington, New Orleans and the road
title: The Dew Drop's owner and back to Texas one-nighters with Ray Charles and Charles Brown
summary: Frank Painia and his brothers ran the Dew Drop; Turner then played one-nighters in Texas on bills with Ray Charles, the Clovers and Drifters.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Well, anyway, gettin' back to this Creole business. The fellow that run the place was named Frank Peffe [pronounces the name "Pen-yay"]. He had about four...five brothers, and they all worked in the place, an' we had a good time. We had...I used to go down there a beautiful time o' year. Ever' time I'd leave an' go away, they'd call me back...'cause we'd pack the place.
An' so I left outa New Orleans and went back down in Texas. So I played some one-nighters. I'm down the highway with Ray Charles an' Charles Brown...the Clovers...
Was Pete Johnson still with you when you were doin' this?

Uh huh. The Drifters an' ssss..."Momma Treats Your Daughter Mean"...Fay Adams...an' all these people...Hazel Scott...an' all these people we worked with. It's practically all over the country we played.
